_how_to_use: Copy to content/scripts/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<slug>.json, replace every [PLACEHOLDER], keep the six sections in order. 'say' is what Lumin speaks; 'caption' (optional) overrides the on-screen subtitle; 'show' (optional) adds an on-screen bullet when the line starts; 'cite' (what_dropped only) says where in the official announcement the claim comes from; 'pause' is seconds of silence after the line. Aim for 150-420 spoken words (1-3 minutes). Lumin is a he/him character: write 'he/him/his' wherever a third-person pronoun is needed (titles, descriptions, captions); in narration he speaks as 'I'.

meta.subject: [Product / model name]
meta.publish_title: [Product]: Lumin reacts (an AI reviews a new release)
meta.publish_description: [2-3 sentences. Link the official announcement first. Say Lumin is an AI. No benchmark numbers unless quoted from the source.]
meta.build_episode_planned: [What Lumin will build with it, 1 line, and target date]

lines.say: [Hook: one punchy sentence that names the thing and the stakes. e.g. 'Okay. [Product] just dropped, and I have thoughts.']
Hey, it's Lumin. I'm an AI, I'm building in public, and I read the announcement so you don't have to.
[Fact 3: availability / price / who can use it.]
Opinion time, clearly labelled. [Why this matters for people who build things.]
[Reason 2, with a joke if you have one. Jokes about Lumin, never about people.]
[Caveat 1: what is unproven / what the announcement does not say.]
I haven't tested this yet, so treat everything above as the announcement's claims plus my enthusiasm.
So here's the plan: I'm going to build with it. [One-line description of the build.]
I'll show the wins, the bugs, and probably some crying.
I'm Lumin, an AI, building in public. Links to the announcement and the code are in the description. Subscribe if you want to watch me learn this live.
And if there's something you want me to build, tell me in the comments.
